claim: The Linus Pauling Institute recommends that generally healthy adults take 2,000 IU of supplemental vitamin D3 daily, and specifically emphasizes this for older adults over 50
stance_target: Briyo Vitamin D3 2000 IU dosage appropriateness
scope_conditions: LPI recommendation for healthy adults; United States context; last updated 2021
quoted_support: The Linus Pauling Institute (LPI) recommends that generally healthy adults take 2,000 IU (50 μg) of supplemental vitamin D daily. Daily supplementation with 2,000 IU (50 μg) of vitamin D is especially important for older adults because aging is associated with a reduced capacity to synthesize vitamin D in the skin upon sun exposure.

claim: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is the preferred form for supplementation over vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol), being more efficacious in maintaining 25(OH)D concentrations
stance_target: D3 softgel form used in Briyo supplement
scope_conditions: 25-week double-blind RCT and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing D2 vs D3
quoted_support: A 25-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial found daily supplementation with 1,000 IU of vitamin D3 initiated at the end of summer to be more efficacious than vitamin D2 in maintaining summertime concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D during fall and winter months.
numbers: 1000 IU/day D3 superior to D2 in 25-week RCT
D3 better than D2 for bolus dosing per meta-analysis

claim: Vitamin D toxicity (hypercalcemia) is unlikely in healthy people at intake levels lower than 10,000 IU/day; hypercalcemia has been observed following daily doses greater than 50,000 IU
stance_target: Safety of 2000 IU/day Vitamin D3 supplementation
scope_conditions: Multiple clinical studies reviewed; healthy adult populations
quoted_support: Overall, research suggests that vitamin D toxicity is very unlikely in healthy people at intake levels lower than 10,000 IU/day. Hypercalcemia has been observed following daily doses of greater than 50,000 IU of vitamin D.

claim: Vitamin D deficiency causes muscle weakness and pain in both children and adults; 93% of patients with persistent musculoskeletal pain had 25(OH)D ≤20 ng/mL in a clinical study
stance_target: Vitamin D3 muscle function support claims
scope_conditions: Cross-sectional study of 150 consecutive patients with nonspecific musculoskeletal pain referred to Minnesota clinic
quoted_support: Vitamin D deficiency causes muscle weakness and pain in children and adults. In a cross-sectional study of 150 consecutive patients referred to a clinic in Minnesota for the evaluation of persistent, nonspecific musculoskeletal pain, 93% had serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations equal to or below 20 ng/mL, with a mean concentration of 12.1 ng/mL.
numbers: 93% of musculoskeletal pain patients had 25(OH)D ≤20 ng/mL

claim: Randomized clinical trials indicate that supplementation with at least 800 IU/day of vitamin D may reduce the risk of falls and fractures in older individuals
stance_target: Vitamin D3 bone health and fall prevention efficacy
scope_conditions: Multiple RCTs in older adults; combined D+calcium most effective for fracture reduction
quoted_support: Randomized clinical trials indicate that supplementation with at least 800 IU/day of vitamin D may reduce the risk of falls and fractures in older individuals.
numbers: 800 IU/day minimum effective dose for fall/fracture reduction
Meta-analysis: highest D intake (792-2000 IU/day) had 30% lower hip fracture risk and 14% lower non-spine fracture risk

claim: Vitamin D (calcitriol) is a potent immune system modulator; VDR is expressed by most immune cells including T cells, B cells, macrophages and dendritic cells, and vitamin D enhances innate immunity and inhibits autoimmunity
scope_conditions: Laboratory and clinical studies; molecular mechanisms established
quoted_support: Acting through the VDR, 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is a potent immune system modulator. The VDR is expressed by most cells of the immune system, including regulatory T cells and antigen-presenting cells, such as dendritic cells and macrophages. There is considerable scientific evidence that 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D has a variety of effects on immune system function, which may enhance innate immunity and inhibit the development of autoimmunity.
numbers: Immune cells produce their own 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D locally

claim: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults; secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D insufficiency increases bone breakdown and precipitates osteoporosis
stance_target: Vitamin D3 bone health necessity and benefit claims
scope_conditions: Well-established clinical literature; multiple decades of research
quoted_support: Vitamin D is important for normal bone development and maintenance. Severe vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to vitamin D insufficiency can increase bone breakdown and precipitate osteoporosis.
numbers: VDR expressed by osteoblasts and osteoclasts
Calcium absorption requires adequate vitamin D

claim: Dark skin pigmentation significantly reduces vitamin D synthesis from sunlight, making supplementation especially important for dark-skinned populations including Indians
stance_target: Need for Vitamin D supplementation in Indian/South Asian population
scope_conditions: Physiological studies; populations at northern latitudes or with limited sun exposure; India at various latitudes
quoted_support: People with dark-colored skin synthesize markedly less vitamin D on exposure to sunlight than those with lighter complexion. Additionally, older adults have diminished capacity to synthesize vitamin D from sunlight exposure and frequently use sunscreen or protective clothing.
numbers: SPF 10 sunscreen reduces D production by 90%
Min 15 min sun exposure at 25°N latitude needed for 1000 IU synthesis

claim: Optimal serum 25(OH)D target for health benefits is 30-60 ng/mL; observational studies associate this range with lower risks of cancers and autoimmune diseases
stance_target: Justification for regular vitamin D3 supplementation at 2000 IU
scope_conditions: Observational studies; optimal range per LPI 2021 recommendation
quoted_support: Observational studies suggest that serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations between 30 ng/mL and 60 ng/mL are associated with lower risks of adverse health outcomes, including cancers and autoimmune diseases.
